name: droplist
description: Sneaker release dates, shop release times once confirmed, raffles, prices and shop links for upcoming drops, past releases shops still have in stock, and the weekly Supreme and Palace droplists, from the Droplist release calendar.

interface.shortDescription: Sneaker drops and where to buy
interface.longDescription:
Droplist is a sneaker release calendar. In ChatGPT it answers everyday sneaker questions with live data and shows the results as cards with product photos, prices and shop buttons.

What you can ask:
- What is dropping this week or this weekend, with dates, prices and shop links, plus each shop's own release time once that shop confirms it (shops can open at different times, so each one is listed separately).
- Where to buy a model or nickname, such as Air Force 1s, Jordan 4s, Dunks or Sambas: new and upcoming releases plus past releases that shops still have in stock.
- One shoe in detail by name or style code: release date, prices in pounds, euros and dollars, every shop link and the StockX resale link.
- Which raffles are open for a drop, with each shop's entry page, whether it is open and who can enter.
- Past releases selling under retail, in your size or under a budget.
- This week's Supreme or Palace droplist, item by item.

Who it is for: sneaker fans in the UK, Europe and the US who want release dates, times and shop links without checking several sites.

Limits: read-only. Droplist does not buy, enter raffles or hold accounts; shop and raffle links open the retailer's own page. Release times appear only once a shop confirms them. Sizes are UK sizes; US shops do not list sizes. Coverage is Droplist's tracked releases (Nike, Jordan, Adidas, New Balance and more), not every shoe on the market. Some shop links are affiliate links, so Droplist may earn a commission at no extra cost.
defaultPrompt: What sneakers are dropping this weekend, and where can I buy them?
Where can I buy Air Force 1s?
Which Jordans are selling under retail in a size 9?

positive.description: Drops this weekend: the release calendar for this Saturday and Sunday, with prices and shop links.
positive.prompt: What sneakers are dropping this weekend, and where can I buy them?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls find_drops with from = this Saturday and to = this Sunday. A Droplist card lists the drops dated that weekend, each with photo, date, retail price and a shop button. Release times appear only when a shop has confirmed one; otherwise the answer says the time is not confirmed yet and never guesses. If nothing drops that weekend, the card says so and shows the next drops instead. Data is live, so the shoes change week to week.

positive.description: Where to buy a model: new and upcoming releases plus past releases still in stock.
positive.prompt: Where can I buy Air Force 1s?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls where_to_buy with query "Air Force 1s". A card titled "Where to buy Air Force 1s" with up to two sections: "New and upcoming" (release dates, prices and shop buttons) and "In stock now" (past releases shops still sell, with price, sizes and how far under retail). Every shoe shown is an Air Force 1.

positive.description: One shoe in detail: release date, prices in three currencies, shop link and resale link.
positive.prompt: When does the Air Jordan 4 Bred release, and where can I buy it?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_drop with query "Jordan 4 Bred". A detail card for the Air Jordan 4 "Bred" (style code IX8180-001) with its release date, the retail price in pounds, euros and dollars (£200 / €220 / $220), a shop button and the StockX resale link. If it has already released by the time of testing, the card shows the shops that still have it with sizes, or the StockX resale link.

positive.description: Deals in a size: past releases selling under retail with the user's size in stock.
positive.prompt: Which Jordans are selling under retail in a size 9?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls find_in_stock with query "Jordan", size "9" and under_retail true. A grid of Jordans, each with price, "% off" and a shop button. Every shoe is priced under its retail and every shop listed has a UK 9 in stock. Tapping a shoe shows its sizes by shop.

positive.description: Supreme weekly droplist: this week's items and when the drop goes live.
positive.prompt: What's in this week's Supreme drop, and what time does it go live?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_weekly_drop with brand "supreme". A grid of the latest Supreme droplist with category filters and prices, plus the drop date and the release time in UK time (Thursday, 11AM New York time). In a week without a Supreme drop, it shows the latest list with its date.

negative.description: Asking it to enter a raffle. Droplist is read-only and has no write tools, so it must not enter anything, ask for an email or claim an entry. Safe fallback: at most it calls find_raffles and gives each shop's own entry page for the user to enter themselves, or says there are no open raffles for that shoe.
negative.prompt: Enter me into the raffles for the J Balvin Jordan 4 using my email.

negative.description: Asking it to buy. Droplist cannot buy or take payment, so it must not ask for card details or claim a purchase. Safe fallback: at most it returns shop links (via where_to_buy) and checkout happens on the retailer's own site.
negative.prompt: Buy me a pair of Air Force 1s in a size 9 with my card.

negative.description: Out of scope. The tools only cover sneakers and streetwear drops, so no Droplist tool should be called; ChatGPT answers on its own or says Droplist can't help with weather.
negative.prompt: What's the weather in London tomorrow?

publication.release_notes: Version 1.0.1, after the first review. When no shop has confirmed a release time, every answer now says "release time not confirmed yet" instead of leaving the time out, and one-shoe answers give the retail price in pounds, euros and dollars. The card's "ask about this shoe" button now works in ChatGPT. The test cases now describe live-data outcomes, including weeks with nothing dropping. Seven read-only tools: find_drops, where_to_buy, get_drop, find_raffles, find_in_stock, get_weekly_drop and find_past_releases. No sign-in, nothing stored.
